final_proof:
Let \(h=\frac12\bigl(f+g-|f-g|\bigr)\). We prove that \(f\wedge g=h\) by showing that the two functions have the same value at every point of \(S\). (The phrase “pointwise maximum” in the statement is evidently a typographical error; the displayed definition of \(f\wedge g\) uses the minimum, and that is the definition used here.)

Fix an arbitrary \(s\in S\), and put \(a=f(s)\) and \(b=g(s)\). By the definitions of pointwise addition, subtraction, absolute value, and scalar multiplication,
\[
h(s)=\frac12\bigl(a+b-|a-b|\bigr).
\]
Since the order on \(\mathbb R\) is total, either \(a\le b\) or \(b<a\).

If \(a\le b\), then \(a-b\le0\), so \(|a-b|=-(a-b)=b-a\). Therefore
\[
h(s)=\frac12\bigl(a+b-(b-a)\bigr)=\frac12(2a)=a.
\]
In this case \(\min\{a,b\}=a\), and hence \(h(s)=a=(f\wedge g)(s)\).

If \(b<a\), then \(a-b>0\), so \(|a-b|=a-b\). Therefore
\[
h(s)=\frac12\bigl(a+b-(a-b)\bigr)=\frac12(2b)=b.
\]
In this case \(\min\{a,b\}=b\), and hence \(h(s)=b=(f\wedge g)(s)\).

Thus \(h(s)=(f\wedge g)(s)\) for every \(s\in S\). By extensionality of functions,
\[
f\wedge g=h=\frac12\bigl(f+g-|f-g|\bigr),
\]
as claimed.
